elements.scope_reason: 'Treat as anaphylaxis' is the conclusion of the delayed-collapse branch; the house standard encodes it as a probable Anaphylaxis diagnosis rule from the branch criteria.
parts_missing: Delayed-collapse timing (5-10 min, up to 1 hour after vaccination) not encoded or declared not_representable
Loss of consciousness > 1 minute and not relieved by lying down not encoded
BP 'remains low' (persistence) not encoded; only a single low reading
Anaphylaxis branch is a flat OR, so any single sign (e.g. cough alone) after collapse+vaccination yields probable anaphylaxis, whereas the page lists the features together as a pattern
elements.problem: Core criteria (BP <90/60, pulse >120, wheeze, stridor, cough, swelling, rash) are encoded with correct thresholds and units and right concepts; the temporal/duration discriminators of the branch are absent. 'Eruption' (morphologic abnormality) is a weak stand-in for 'rash'; a finding such as Rash may be closer.
evidence: Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after collapse following vaccination :: (and (clinical_finding Collapse) (clinical_finding Vaccination given) (or (< SBP 90) (< DBP 60) (> Pulse 120) Wheezing Stridor Cough Swelling Eruption))

rule_level_problems.rule: task Check for collapse following vaccination features
rule_level_problems.problem: check_for omits Systolic BP, Diastolic BP and Pulse, which both diagnosis rules use; a clinician is not prompted to record them. The page explicitly says to check breathing, pulse and BP.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: Fainting criteria from outside box (sudden onset at time of vaccination; LOC 20 s to 1 min; no other signs) only partly captured: timing and LOC duration absent; 'Vaccination given' is used as proxy for timing. BP requires a recorded measurement, so with BP missing fainting cannot fire. Hyperventilation (allowed) is not excluded, fine. Page says 'BP briefly low but rapidly normal', which the rule encodes as currently normal; acceptable.

Branches are complementary except when vitals are missing; if no vitals and no symptoms are recorded neither fires, and if a symptom is present only anaphylaxis fires. Not contradictory, but note the fainting rule's Syncope concept for a collapse presentation is reasonable.
Refer-if items (head injury, heart condition, unusual symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, confusion) are management/referral, out of scope by design. Fine.

summary: The page has a single red-box element (Treat as anaphylaxis), encoded as a probable anaphylaxis rule with correct BP, pulse and sign thresholds but without the delayed-onset and LOC-duration discriminators and with an any-one-sign OR. The check_for list omits the BP and pulse measurements used by both rules. SNOMED concepts exist and mean what the page says, though 'Eruption' is a loose match for 'rash'.
